48.original: Come again? A sin eater fused with a voidsent?

50.original: Tell me. You were investigating a ruined church of the First Light?

51.original: You possess a singular talent for dredging up memories I'd sooner forget.

52.original: ...Not that I can fault you for it. Remembrance is the burden of the living.

53.original: What you described sounds like a voidsent I once defeated in the Thirteenth. Back before...any of this.

54.original: At the time, I was just another memoriate, traveling the land and hunting the monsters that preyed upon the innocent.

55.original: ...Until I realized one such monster could be of use to me.

56.original: When I sealed it in memoria, I had no other thought but preventing its resuscitation.

57.original: But when I agreed to journey to the First as the Ascians' hidden emissary, I remembered that voidsent.

58.original: A creature of its caliber could turn the tide of battle. It could lend me the strength I needed to prevail.

59.original: Drawing its power from the memoria would have been a simple matter.

60.original: Yet after bringing it here, I left it to gather dust upon my desk in Lakeland.

61.original: If I truly had wanted to defeat Ardbert, that voidsent would have been my solution...

62.original: But I was afraid. Afraid of being twisted by Darkness like so many memoriates before me. Afraid of becoming what I hated the most.

63.original: Never mind that it was far too late. The Ascians' puppet, fearing corruption... Absurd, don't you think?

66.original: Part of you always wanted Ardbert to succeed?

68.original: You are kind to say so.

69.original: Succeed in slaying the monster, you mean? I wish I had. Would that I'd been a traitor only to myself─I could've believed my heart was in the right place, if nothing else.

70.original: Absurd, yet in no way amusing. I agree.

71.original: Above all, I was naive to think that the memoria would be safe in my former quarters, even once they were rendered inaccessible to mortal interlopers.

72.original: Sin eaters must have been drawn to the memoria's concentrated Darkness. They would have provided enough Light to break the seal─and suitable fodder for the fiend in its newfound freedom.

73.original: In sparing the First from its wrath, you have prevented untold devastation.

74.original: I know that words will not absolve me. Yet, as one who draws breath upon this star, I offer them nonetheless.

75.original: Warrior of Darkness... Nay, Warrior of Light. I thank you.
